summary: Iteration 55 backend-only verification of the `id`-index fix. Confirmed id_1 indexes exist on bills, users, brands, stores, campaigns, coupons, staff, staff_incentives; verified bills.id lookups now use IXSCAN (no COLLSCAN) via explain; verified GET /api/bills/{id}/image (valid=200, unknown=404), repeated image calls, and POST /api/admin/bills/{id}/edit-brand?reprocess=false all complete well under the 500ms budget; confirmed ensure_db_indexes() is idempotent both in-process and across a real supervisor backend restart. Re-ran the full iteration_54 regression suite: no regressions. Total 29/29 backend tests passed.

minor.issue: Benign pre-existing WARNING on every boot: 'Index otp_codes.phone skip / blocked_phones.phone skip — IndexKeySpecsConflict' because those collections already have a UNIQUE phone_1 index while the spec requests a non-unique one. Harmless but noisy; consider naming or marking those specs unique.

Collections still queried by find_one({'id': ...}) without an id index: parking_sessions (growing), sync_jobs, bulk_reprocess_jobs, app_settings. parking_sessions in particular can grow large on production and will hit the same COLLSCAN timeout pattern.

action_items: Optional hardening before prod redeploy: add ('parking_sessions','id'), ('sync_jobs','id'), ('bulk_reprocess_jobs','id') to ensure_db_indexes() to prevent the same COLLSCAN timeout on those paths.
Optional: silence the otp_codes.phone / blocked_phones.phone IndexKeySpecsConflict boot warnings by declaring them unique in index_specs.
Production: redeploy is required — the index creation runs at backend startup, so Atlas will only get id_1 after deploy. Verify post-deploy with db.bills.getIndexes() on Atlas.
critical_code_review_comments: ensure_db_indexes() correctly creates each index independently inside try/except so one conflict cannot block the rest — good. Verified via boot logs that failures are warnings only and 'DB indexes ensured' still logs.

Index creation at startup is fine for small/medium collections, but on a large production bills collection createIndex is foreground-blocking on the collection; if bills grows very large consider creating the index out-of-band on Atlas first.
seed_data_creation: One temporary bill doc id prefix TEST-I55-* with an inline base64 image; deleted in fixture teardown (verified 0 leftovers). Iteration_54 suite seeds/cleans its own TEST-I54-* docs (verified 0 leftovers).
test_credentials: Admin: admin / CP67Admin@2025 (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md) — login works, returns token.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Perf/index suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration55_id_indexes_perf.py (index existence per collection, explain-plan IXSCAN check, <500ms latency budget on image + edit-brand, ensure_db_indexes idempotency). Note edit-brand payload field is `new_store_name`, not `brand_name`. Preview bills collection is tiny (18 docs) so latency numbers here are not a proxy for production Atlas volume — the explain-plan IXSCAN assertion is the meaningful signal.
rca_of_the_issue: bills had no index on the application-level `id` field, so every find_one({'id': bill_id}) was a COLLSCAN; on production Atlas with growing volume this exceeded the pymongo socket read timeout and surfaced as fetch_error 'read operation timed out' in /api/bills/{id}/image. Fix (id_1 indexes added in ensure_db_indexes) is verified in preview: explain now shows IXSCAN for bills.id and all 8 target collections have id_1.
